paragraphs.text: Training-data attribution is typically validated against content-similarity proxies rather than causal effects known in advance. We therefore install per-source effects by fine-tuning, measure each against a retrained control, remove each method’s top-ranked documents, and retrain. This exploratory study examines factory farming with Qwen3-4B, gradient-based removal methods, and paired training seeds for the declared seed-paired families; other readings are labeled separately. The same premise specification produced a 22x range of installed effects across surface forms, from +0.0072 for long articles at the two-epoch reading to +0.1574 for short answers, although the pair also differs in premise density and voice. Factorial cells were separately estimated corpus arms, and their ratios were point-estimate comparisons rather than tested effects. In the evaluated cells, oracle removal, a recorded positive-control contrast rather than a candidate method, recovered attributable fractions of +0.52 and +0.62 at the twenty-percent budget. By contrast, removal guided by the single-final-checkpoint TracIn implementation increased the effect at both seeds at the ten-percent budget, with attributable fractions of -0.91 and -0.42 and intervals excluding zero. These removability and detection inferences are cell-local.
